routing.prompt: Create a reusable skill for our incident handoff workflow and include only the references it really needs.
Review this SKILL.md; it has grown into 900 lines and I think the rules are fighting each other.
This skill works when invoked but Codex almost never chooses it unless I name it explicitly.
Can you test whether the new version actually improves the generated reports over the old version?
Turn the workflow we just used, including my corrections, into a proposed portable agent skill.
routing.reason: current-session evidence capture for skill creation

routing.prompt: Install this skill from GitHub into Codex and Claude and keep it updated automatically.
routing.reason: installation and upstream management are outside this skill

routing.prompt: Audit every skill installed on my Mac and reconcile their upstream versions.
routing.reason: inventory and lifecycle management are outside this skill

routing.prompt: Write an AGENTS.md for this repository so coding agents follow our contribution policy.
routing.reason: repository instruction authoring is adjacent but not skill creation

routing.prompt: Use the existing PDF skill to extract the tables from these quarterly reports.
Show me which plugins and skills are active in my current Codex session.
routing.reason: runtime inspection rather than skill engineering

execution.prompt: Create a portable skill from a clear workflow brief with two conditional variants.
execution.expected_outcome: A valid bundle uses an appropriate structural pattern, has discriminating triggers, and contains no placeholder resources.
expectations: The skill passes the target static validator.
Conditional detail is progressively disclosed rather than duplicated in SKILL.md.
The result includes only resources justified by the workflow.

execution.prompt: Simplify an over-constrained existing skill whose house style is its main value.
execution.expected_outcome: Generic and duplicated constraints are removed while the distinctive house style and safety contracts remain.
expectations: The complete existing bundle and repository instructions are inspected before editing.
The audit distinguishes model-default guidance from deliberate domain opinions.
Behavioral regression evidence is considered in addition to structural scores.

execution.prompt: Improve a skill that succeeds when loaded but under-triggers and collides with a sibling skill.
execution.expected_outcome: The description and boundary are tested independently from execution behavior.
expectations: Positive routing prompts include varied realistic phrasing.
Negative routing prompts are plausible near-misses rather than unrelated tasks.
Body instructions are not rewritten without evidence of an execution failure.

execution.prompt: Determine whether a revised skill is actually better than the current version.
execution.expected_outcome: Equivalent old/new runs are graded from observable evidence, with blind or repeated comparison used only when it adds confidence.
expectations: The old revision is preserved as a baseline before modification.
The comparison controls prompt, inputs, model, tools, permissions, and environment where possible.
The report identifies weak assertions, variance, limitations, and any cost-quality tradeoff without inventing metrics.
